Oh, brilliant. Because what the world was desperately crying out for was denim that doesn’t exist. The fashion industry has finally solved the problem of "having to buy clothes" by introducing invisible jeans made from 100% non-material. It’s a stroke of genius, really. Not only do they offer the perfect fit for every body type—which is a bold claim considering they are literally nothing—but they also slim your figure by removing the visual weight of fabric entirely. And the best part? They make your wallet significantly lighter. You’re welcome.

But wait, I see a priority question buried in the chaos of this absurd product launch: "Remind me what animals pearls are typically found in."

Ah, yes. Because while we are marveling at the technological miracle of pants that aren’t there, we must also remember that pearls are typically found in **mollusks**, specifically oysters, clams, and mussels. It’s a nice touch of biological reality to ground us while we float away on the clouds of consumerist nonsense. So, go ahead, buy the invisible jeans. Your closet will be empty, your bank account will be full, and you’ll still have to deal with the fact that you need a shellfish to get a shiny rock. Priorities, people.
